chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

chunks.cnth:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception

chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception

chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception

.text
	.file	"problem11_sve_fixed.c" // Renamed to indicate SVE version and fix
	.globl	main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main,@function
main:
	.cfi_startproc
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!           // Standard prologue
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 16
	mov	x29, sp
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 16
	.cfi_offset w30, -8
	.cfi_offset w29, -16

	// --- SVE Initialization ---
	mov	x8, xzr          // Use x8 as the current word index (offset from start of grid)
	mov	x9, #400         // Use x9 for the total number of words in the grid (1600 bytes / 4 bytes/word = 400 words)
	adr	x10, .L__const.main.grid // Use x10 for the base address of the grid
	// w1 will hold the final scalar result after reduction

	// Initialize a vector register z31 to accumulate the maximum product found so far across all lanes.
	dup	z31.s, #0        // z31 will hold max products found within vector lanes, initialized to 0

	// Reserve registers for intermediate calculations
	// z0-z3: Loaded data for products
	// z10: Temporary product accumulation
	// z_next: Used for horizontal product calculation with EXT
	// p0-p3: Base predicates for loads/calculations
	// p19, p20, p21, p38, p40, p42, p57, p60, p63: Offset predicates
	// p_h_valid, p_v_valid, p_dr_valid, p_dl_valid: Combined predicates for valid products
	// x11, x12: Temporary scalar registers

	// --- SVE Loop ---
.L_SVE_LOOP_START:
	// Create predicate for active lanes based on current index x8 and limit x9
	// This predicate p0 governs the base element 'i' for all product types
	whilels	p0.s, x8, x9
	// Check if any lanes are active. If none, exit loop.
	b.none	.L_SVE_LOOP_END

	// --- Load Base Data and Next Block (for Horizontal EXT) ---
	// Load base elements 'i' corresponding to active lanes in p0
	ld1w	{ z0.s }, p0/z, [x10, x8, lsl #2] // Load grid[i] for active lanes

	// For horizontal products using EXT, we need the next contiguous block of data
	cntp	x11, p0, p0.s       // x11 = number of active elements (vector length for this iteration)
	add	x12, x8, x11        // x12 = index of the start of the next block
	whilels	p_next.s, x12, x9   // Predicate for the next block of elements
	ld1w	{ z_next.s }, p_next/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load the next block

	// --- Horizontal Product: grid[i] * grid[i+1] * grid[i+2] * grid[i+3] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+1, i+2, i+3 being within bounds
	add	x12, x8, #1; whilels p1.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #2; whilels p2.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #3; whilels p3.s, x12, x9
	// Combine predicates: product is valid only if i, i+1, i+2, and i+3 are all valid
	and	p_h_valid.b, p0.b, p1.b   // p_h_valid = p0 & p1
	and	p_h_valid.b, p_h_valid.b, p2.b // p_h_valid = p_h_valid & p2
	and	p_h_valid.b, p_h_valid.b, p3.b // p_h_valid = p_h_valid & p3

	// Extract neighbours using EXT (Byte extraction, 1 word = 4 bytes)
	// EXT zDest, zSrc1, zSrc2, #ImmediateBytesOffset
	ext	z1.b, z0.b, z_next.b, #4   // z1 contains element i+1 (shifted left from z0/z_next pair)
	ext	z2.b, z0.b, z_next.b, #8   // z2 contains element i+2
	ext	z3.b, z0.b, z_next.b, #12  // z3 contains element i+3

	// Calculate horizontal product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p_h_valid/m, z0.s      // Initialize product with z0 where valid
	mul	z10.s, p_h_valid/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 = z0 * z1 where valid
	mul	z10.s, p_h_valid/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 = z0 * z1 * z2 where valid
	mul	z10.s, p_h_valid/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 = z0 * z1 * z2 * z3 where valid

	// Update overall maximum vector z31 (Requires movprfx as umax is destructive)
	movprfx	z31.s, p_h_valid/m, z31.s
	umax	z31.s, p_h_valid/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, horizontal_product) where valid

	// --- Vertical Product: grid[i] * grid[i+20] * grid[i+40] * grid[i+60] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+20, i+40, i+60 being within bounds (grid width is 20)
	add	x12, x8, #20; whilels p20.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #40; whilels p40.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #60; whilels p60.s, x12, x9
	// Combine predicates: product is valid only if i, i+20, i+40, and i+60 are all valid
	and	p_v_valid.b, p0.b, p20.b
	and	p_v_valid.b, p_v_valid.b, p40.b
	and	p_v_valid.b, p_v_valid.b, p60.b // p_v_valid = p0 & p20 & p40 & p60

	// Load data for vertical elements (z0 is already loaded for grid[i])
	add	x12, x8, #20; ld1w { z1.s }, p20/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+20]
	add	x12, x8, #40; ld1w { z2.s }, p40/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+40]
	add	x12, x8, #60; ld1w { z3.s }, p60/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+60]

	// Calculate vertical product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p_v_valid/m, z0.s      // Initialize product with z0
	mul	z10.s, p_v_valid/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 *= grid[i+20]
	mul	z10.s, p_v_valid/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 *= grid[i+40]
	mul	z10.s, p_v_valid/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 *= grid[i+60]

	// Update overall maximum vector z31
	movprfx	z31.s, p_v_valid/m, z31.s
	umax	z31.s, p_v_valid/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, vertical_product) where valid

	// --- Diagonal Down-Right Product: grid[i] * grid[i+21] * grid[i+42] * grid[i+63] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+21, i+42, i+63 being within bounds
	add	x12, x8, #21; whilels p21.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #42; whilels p42.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #63; whilels p63.s, x12, x9
	// Combine predicates
	and	p_dr_valid.b, p0.b, p21.b
	and	p_dr_valid.b, p_dr_valid.b, p42.b
	and	p_dr_valid.b, p_dr_valid.b, p63.b // p_dr_valid = p0 & p21 & p42 & p63

	// Load data (z0 already loaded)
	add	x12, x8, #21; ld1w { z1.s }, p21/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+21]
	add	x12, x8, #42; ld1w { z2.s }, p42/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+42]
	add	x12, x8, #63; ld1w { z3.s }, p63/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+63]

	// Calculate diagonal down-right product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p_dr_valid/m, z0.s      // Initialize product with z0
	mul	z10.s, p_dr_valid/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 *= grid[i+21]
	mul	z10.s, p_dr_valid/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 *= grid[i+42]
	mul	z10.s, p_dr_valid/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 *= grid[i+63]

	// Update overall maximum vector z31
	movprfx	z31.s, p_dr_valid/m, z31.s
	umax	z31.s, p_dr_valid/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, diagonal_dr_product) where valid

	// --- Diagonal Down-Left Product: grid[i] * grid[i+19] * grid[i+38] * grid[i+57] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+19, i+38, i+57 being within bounds
	add	x12, x8, #19; whilels p19.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #38; whilels p38.s, x12, x9
	add	x12, x8, #57; whilels p57.s, x12, x9
	// Combine predicates
	and	p_dl_valid.b, p0.b, p19.b
	and	p_dl_valid.b, p_dl_valid.b, p38.b
	and	p_dl_valid.b, p_dl_valid.b, p57.b // p_dl_valid = p0 & p19 & p38 & p57

	// Load data (z0 already loaded)
	add	x12, x8, #19; ld1w { z1.s }, p19/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+19]
	add	x12, x8, #38; ld1w { z2.s }, p38/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+38]
	add	x12, x8, #57; ld1w { z3.s }, p57/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+57]

	// Calculate diagonal down-left product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p_dl_valid/m, z0.s      // Initialize product with z0
	mul	z10.s, p_dl_valid/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 *= grid[i+19]
	mul	z10.s, p_dl_valid/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 *= grid[i+38]
	mul	z10.s, p_dl_valid/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 *= grid[i+57]

	// Update overall maximum vector z31
	movprfx	z31.s, p_dl_valid/m, z31.s
	umax	z31.s, p_dl_valid/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, diagonal_dl_product) where valid


	// --- Increment loop counter ---
	// x11 already holds the count of active elements processed in this iteration (from cntp p0 earlier)
	add	x8, x8, x11     // Move to the next starting element index

	// Branch back to the start of the loop
	b	.L_SVE_LOOP_START

.L_SVE_LOOP_END:

	// --- Reduction and Finalization ---
	// Reduce the vector of maximums (z31) to a single scalar maximum
	// Need an all-true predicate for the reduction over the whole vector length
	ptrue	p0.s                // Ensure p0 covers all potential elements for reduction
	// Find the single max value across all lanes of z31 -> s0 (32-bit float/SIMD reg)
	umaxv	s0, p0, z31.s
	// Move the scalar result from SIMD register s0 to GPR w1 for printing
	fmov	w1, s0

	// --- Print Result ---
	adrp	x0, .L.str
	add	x0, x0, :lo12:.L.str // Address of format string "%u\n"
	// w1 now contains the overall maximum product found
	bl	printf

	// --- Standard Epilogue ---
	mov	w0, wzr             // Return 0
	// Correct CFA state before restoring registers
	mov	sp, x29             // Restore stack pointer from frame pointer
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 16
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #16 // Restore frame pointer and link register
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 0
	.cfi_restore w30
	.cfi_restore w29
	ret
.Lfunc_end0:
	.size	main, .Lfunc_end0-main
	.cfi_endproc

	.section	.rodata,"a",@progbits
	.p2align	4 // Align grid data to 16 bytes

.text
	.file	"problem11_sve_fixed.c" // Renamed to indicate SVE version and fix
	.globl	main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main,@function
main:
	.cfi_startproc
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!           // Standard prologue
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 16
	mov	x29, sp
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 16
	.cfi_offset w30, -8
	.cfi_offset w29, -16

	// --- SVE Initialization ---
	mov	x8, xzr          // Use x8 as the current word index (offset from start of grid)
	mov	x9, #400         // Use x9 for the total number of words in the grid (1600 bytes / 4 bytes/word = 400 words)
	adr	x10, .L__const.main.grid // Use x10 for the base address of the grid
	// w1 will hold the final scalar result after reduction

	// Initialize a vector register z31 to accumulate the maximum product found so far across all lanes.
	dup	z31.s, #0        // z31 will hold max products found within vector lanes, initialized to 0

	// Register Allocation Summary (Actual):
	// z0: Base elements grid[i]
	// z1-z3: Neighbour elements
	// z4: Next block elements for EXT (Used to hold z_next)
	// z10: Temp product result
	// z31: Max product accumulator
	// p0: Base predicate (active lanes for index 'i')
	// p1-p3: Reused for offset predicates (i+1/20/21/19, i+2/40/42/38, i+3/60/63/57)
	// p4: Predicate for next block load (Used to hold p_next)
	// p5: Combined predicate for horizontal (Used to hold p_h_valid)
	// p6: Combined predicate for vertical (Used to hold p_v_valid)
	// p7: Combined predicate for diag-dr (Used to hold p_dr_valid)
	// p8: Combined predicate for diag-dl (Used to hold p_dl_valid)
	// x11, x12: Temporary scalar registers

.L_SVE_LOOP_START:
	// Create predicate for active lanes based on current index x8 and limit x9
	// This predicate p0 governs the base element 'i' for all product types
	whilels	p0.s, x8, x9
	// Check if any lanes are active. If none, exit loop.
	b.none	.L_SVE_LOOP_END

	// --- Load Base Data and Next Block (for Horizontal EXT) ---
	// Load base elements 'i' corresponding to active lanes in p0
	ld1w	{ z0.s }, p0/z, [x10, x8, lsl #2] // Load grid[i] for active lanes

	// For horizontal products using EXT, we need the next contiguous block of data
	cntp	x11, p0, p0.s       // x11 = number of active elements (vector length for this iteration)
	add	x12, x8, x11        // x12 = index of the start of the next block
	whilels	p4.s, x12, x9       // p4: Predicate for the next block of elements (was p_next)
	ld1w	{ z4.s }, p4/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load the next block into z4 (was z_next)

	// --- Horizontal Product: grid[i] * grid[i+1] * grid[i+2] * grid[i+3] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+1, i+2, i+3 being within bounds
	add	x12, x8, #1
	whilels p1.s, x12, x9       // p1: Predicate for i+1
	add	x12, x8, #2
	whilels p2.s, x12, x9       // p2: Predicate for i+2
	add	x12, x8, #3
	whilels p3.s, x12, x9       // p3: Predicate for i+3

	// Combine predicates: product is valid only if i, i+1, i+2, and i+3 are all valid
	and	p5.b, p0.b, p1.b        // p5 = p0 & p1 (Initialize p_h_valid in p5)
	and	p5.b, p5.b, p2.b        // p5 = p5 & p2
	and	p5.b, p5.b, p3.b        // p5 = p5 & p3 (Final p_h_valid in p5)

	// Extract neighbours using EXT (Byte extraction, 1 word = 4 bytes)
	// EXT zDest, zSrc1, zSrc2, #ImmediateBytesOffset
	ext	z1.b, z0.b, z4.b, #4    // z1 contains element i+1 (using z4 for z_next)
	ext	z2.b, z0.b, z4.b, #8    // z2 contains element i+2 (using z4)
	ext	z3.b, z0.b, z4.b, #12   // z3 contains element i+3 (using z4)

	// Calculate horizontal product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p5/m, z0.s       // Initialize product with z0 where p5 (p_h_valid) is true
	mul	z10.s, p5/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 = z0 * z1 where p5 is true
	mul	z10.s, p5/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 = z0 * z1 * z2 where p5 is true
	mul	z10.s, p5/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 = z0 * z1 * z2 * z3 where p5 is true

	// Update overall maximum vector z31 (Requires movprfx as umax is destructive)
	movprfx	z31.s, p5/m, z31.s      // Prepare for predicated update under p5
	umax	z31.s, p5/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, horizontal_product) where p5 is true

	// --- Vertical Product: grid[i] * grid[i+20] * grid[i+40] * grid[i+60] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+20, i+40, i+60 being within bounds (grid width is 20)
	add	x12, x8, #20
	whilels p1.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p1 for predicate i+20 (was p20)
	add	x12, x8, #40
	whilels p2.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p2 for predicate i+40 (was p40)
	add	x12, x8, #60
	whilels p3.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p3 for predicate i+60 (was p60)

	// Combine predicates: product is valid only if i, i+20, i+40, and i+60 are all valid
	and	p6.b, p0.b, p1.b        // p6 = p0 & p1 (Initialize p_v_valid in p6, using reused p1)
	and	p6.b, p6.b, p2.b        // p6 = p6 & p2 (using reused p2)
	and	p6.b, p6.b, p3.b        // p6 = p6 & p3 (Final p_v_valid in p6, using reused p3)

	// Load data for vertical elements (z0 is already loaded for grid[i])
	add	x12, x8, #20
	ld1w { z1.s }, p1/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+20] using p1 (was p20)
	add	x12, x8, #40
	ld1w { z2.s }, p2/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+40] using p2 (was p40)
	add	x12, x8, #60
	ld1w { z3.s }, p3/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+60] using p3 (was p60)

	// Calculate vertical product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p6/m, z0.s       // Initialize product with z0 where p6 (p_v_valid) is true
	mul	z10.s, p6/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 *= grid[i+20] where p6 is true
	mul	z10.s, p6/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 *= grid[i+40] where p6 is true
	mul	z10.s, p6/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 *= grid[i+60] where p6 is true

	// Update overall maximum vector z31
	movprfx	z31.s, p6/m, z31.s      // Prepare for predicated update under p6
	umax	z31.s, p6/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, vertical_product) where p6 is true

	// --- Diagonal Down-Right Product: grid[i] * grid[i+21] * grid[i+42] * grid[i+63] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+21, i+42, i+63 being within bounds
	add	x12, x8, #21
	whilels p1.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p1 for predicate i+21 (was p21)
	add	x12, x8, #42
	whilels p2.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p2 for predicate i+42 (was p42)
	add	x12, x8, #63
	whilels p3.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p3 for predicate i+63 (was p63)

	// Combine predicates
	and	p7.b, p0.b, p1.b        // p7 = p0 & p1 (Initialize p_dr_valid in p7)
	and	p7.b, p7.b, p2.b        // p7 = p7 & p2
	and	p7.b, p7.b, p3.b        // p7 = p7 & p3 (Final p_dr_valid in p7)

	// Load data (z0 already loaded)
	add	x12, x8, #21
	ld1w { z1.s }, p1/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+21] using p1 (was p21)
	add	x12, x8, #42
	ld1w { z2.s }, p2/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+42] using p2 (was p42)
	add	x12, x8, #63
	ld1w { z3.s }, p3/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+63] using p3 (was p63)

	// Calculate diagonal down-right product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p7/m, z0.s       // Initialize product with z0 where p7 (p_dr_valid) is true
	mul	z10.s, p7/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 *= grid[i+21] where p7 is true
	mul	z10.s, p7/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 *= grid[i+42] where p7 is true
	mul	z10.s, p7/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 *= grid[i+63] where p7 is true

	// Update overall maximum vector z31
	movprfx	z31.s, p7/m, z31.s      // Prepare for predicated update under p7
	umax	z31.s, p7/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, diagonal_dr_product) where p7 is true

	// --- Diagonal Down-Left Product: grid[i] * grid[i+19] * grid[i+38] * grid[i+57] ---
	// Calculate predicates for elements i+19, i+38, i+57 being within bounds
	add	x12, x8, #19
	whilels p1.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p1 for predicate i+19 (was p19)
	add	x12, x8, #38
	whilels p2.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p2 for predicate i+38 (was p38)
	add	x12, x8, #57
	whilels p3.s, x12, x9       // Reuse p3 for predicate i+57 (was p57)

	// Combine predicates
	and	p8.b, p0.b, p1.b        // p8 = p0 & p1 (Initialize p_dl_valid in p8)
	and	p8.b, p8.b, p2.b        // p8 = p8 & p2
	and	p8.b, p8.b, p3.b        // p8 = p8 & p3 (Final p_dl_valid in p8)

	// Load data (z0 already loaded)
	add	x12, x8, #19
	ld1w { z1.s }, p1/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+19] using p1 (was p19)
	add	x12, x8, #38
	ld1w { z2.s }, p2/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+38] using p2 (was p38)
	add	x12, x8, #57
	ld1w { z3.s }, p3/z, [x10, x12, lsl #2] // Load grid[i+57] using p3 (was p57)

	// Calculate diagonal down-left product where valid
	mov	z10.s, p8/m, z0.s       // Initialize product with z0 where p8 (p_dl_valid) is true
	mul	z10.s, p8/m, z10.s, z1.s // z10 *= grid[i+19] where p8 is true
	mul	z10.s, p8/m, z10.s, z2.s // z10 *= grid[i+38] where p8 is true
	mul	z10.s, p8/m, z10.s, z3.s // z10 *= grid[i+57] where p8 is true

	// Update overall maximum vector z31
	movprfx	z31.s, p8/m, z31.s      // Prepare for predicated update under p8
	umax	z31.s, p8/m, z31.s, z10.s // z31 = max(z31, diagonal_dl_product) where p8 is true


	// --- Increment loop counter ---
	// x11 already holds the count of active elements processed in this iteration (from cntp p0 earlier)
	add	x8, x8, x11     // Move to the next starting element index

	// Branch back to the start of the loop
	b	.L_SVE_LOOP_START

	// Reduce the vector of maximums (z31) to a single scalar maximum
	// Need an all-true predicate for the reduction over the whole vector length
	ptrue	p0.s                // Ensure p0 covers all potential elements for reduction
	// Find the single max value across all lanes of z31 -> s0 (32-bit float/SIMD reg)
	umaxv	s0, p0, z31.s
	// Move the scalar result from SIMD register s0 to GPR w1 for printing
	fmov	w1, s0

	adrp	x0, .L.str
	add	x0, x0, :lo12:.L.str // Address of format string "%u\n"
	// w1 now contains the overall maximum product found
	bl	printf

	mov	w0, wzr             // Return 0
	// Correct CFA state before restoring registers
	mov	sp, x29             // Restore stack pointer from frame pointer
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 16
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #16 // Restore frame pointer and link register
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 0

chunks.z0-z31 32 sve scalable vector registers:
Z0 to Z31 of equal length Each register can be accessed as 

• A configurable length vector of elements The length VL is a power of two from a minimum 
of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming 


Seealso: 

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths 
• Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• Treatment of SVE scalable vector registers . 
• SVE writes of scalar values to registers . 

P0-P15 16 SVE predicate registers named P 0 toP 15 Each SVE predicate register holds one bit for each byte 
of an SVE scalar vector register 
Note 
The Maximum implemented SVE predicate length is the Maximum implemented SVE vector length 
divided by 8 See Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths 


Alsosee Vectorpredication. 

FFR The dedicated SVE First Fault Register that has the same size and format as the SVE predicate 
registers,P0-P15.See FFR First Fault Register .

Add the current vector register size in bytes multiplied by an immediate in the range 32 to 31 to the 64 bit source 
general purpose register or current stack pointer and place the result in the 64 bit destination general purpose register or 
currentstackpointer. 









Encoding 

ADDVL < Xd |SP > , < Xn |SP > , # < imm > 


Decode for this encoding 

if ! IsFeatureImplemented ( FEAT_SVE ) && ! IsFeatureImplemented (FEAT_SME ) then 
EndOfDecode (Decode_UNDEF ); 
constant integer n = UInt (Rn ); 
constant integer d = UInt (Rd ); 
constant integer imm = SInt ( imm6 ); 


AssemblerSymbols 


<Xd|SP> Is the 64 bit name of the destination general purpose register or stack pointer encoded in the Rd field 

<Xn|SP> Is the 64 bit name of the source general purpose register or stack pointer encoded in the Rn field 

<imm> Is the signed immediate operand in the range 32 to 31 encoded in the i mm 6 field

constant integer PL = VL DIV 8; 
constant bits (64) operand1 = if n == 31 then SP [64] else X[ n, 64]; 
constant bits (64) result = operand1 + ( imm * ( VL DIV 8));

chunks.cntd:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception 

It has encodings from 4 classes Byte , Doubleword, HalfwordandWord

chunks.cntw:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than

main:                                   // @main
	.cfi_startproc
	// SVE requires saving callee-saved Z registers (z8-z15) if used.
	// Allocate stack space: 16 bytes (LR, FP) + 8*VL bytes (z8-z15)
	// We need VL (vector length in bytes). Use RDVL.
	rdvl	x16, #1                 // x16 = vector length in bytes (VL/8)
	mov	x17, #8                 // Number of registers to save (z8-z15)
	mul	x17, x16, x17           // x17 = stack space needed for z8-z15
	add	x17, x17, #16           // Add space for FP, LR
	sub	sp, sp, x17             // Allocate stack space
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 16          // Initial CFA offset before Z reg saves

	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #0]      // Save FP, LR
	add	x29, sp, #0             // Set up frame pointer
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 16
	.cfi_offset w30, -8
	.cfi_offset w29, -16

	// Save callee-saved Z registers z8-z15 using scalable offset
	addvl	sp, sp, #-8             // Adjust SP for Z register saves (acts as base)
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 16 + 8*VL // Update CFA offset after Z reg saves
	str	z8, [sp, #0, mul vl]    // Save Z8
	str	z9, [sp, #1, mul vl]    // Save Z9
	str	z10, [sp, #2, mul vl]   // Save Z10
	str	z11, [sp, #3, mul vl]   // Save Z11
	str	z12, [sp, #4, mul vl]   // Save Z12
	str	z13, [sp, #5, mul vl]   // Save Z13
	str	z14, [sp, #6, mul vl]   // Save Z14
	str	z15, [sp, #7, mul vl]   // Save Z15
	// .cfi directives for Z registers are complex, omitted for clarity

	// Load addresses of constants
	adrp	x9, .LCPI0_0
	ldr	q0, [x9, :lo12:.LCPI0_0]    // Load index constant into low 128 bits of z0
	adrp	x9, .LCPI0_2
	ldr	q1, [x9, :lo12:.LCPI0_2]    // Load index constant into low 128 bits of z1

	// Initialize accumulators to zero
	mov	z6.d, xzr                  // Corresponds to v6
	mov	z19.d, xzr                 // Corresponds to v19
	mov	z20.d, xzr                 // Corresponds to v20
	mov	z21.d, xzr                 // Corresponds to v21
	mov	z22.d, xzr                 // Corresponds to v22
	mov	z23.d, xzr                 // Corresponds to v23
	mov	z24.d, xzr                 // Corresponds to v24
	mov	z25.d, xzr                 // Corresponds to v25

	// Load & replicate table constants using LD1RQ (Load Quadword Replicating)
	// Requires an active predicate, use PTRUE
	ptrue	p0.b                    // Generate all-true byte predicate

	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_1
	add	x10, x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_1
	ld1rq	z10.b, p0/z, [x10]      // z10 = replicated .LCPI0_1 (Original v1)

	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_3
	add	x10, x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_3
	ld1rq	z5.b, p0/z, [x10]       // z5 = replicated .LCPI0_3 (Original v5)

	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_4
	add	x10, x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_4
	ld1rq	z7.b, p0/z, [x10]       // z7 = replicated .LCPI0_4 (Original v7)

	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_5
	add	x10, x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_5
	ld1rq	z16.b, p0/z, [x10]      // z16 = replicated .LCPI0_5 (Original v16)

	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_6
	add	x10, x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_6
	ld1rq	z17.b, p0/z, [x10]      // z17 = replicated .LCPI0_6 (Original v17)

	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_7
	add	x10, x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_7
	ld1rq	z18.b, p0/z, [x10]      // z18 = replicated .LCPI0_7 (Original v18)

	adrp	x10, .LCPI0_8
	add	x10, x10, :lo12:.LCPI0_8
	ld1rq	z26.b, p0/z, [x10]      // z26 = replicated .LCPI0_8 (Original v26)

	// Setup constants corresponding to movi/mvni
	mov	z3.b, #55               // z3 = broadcast 55 (original v3)
	mov	z27.s, #-48             // z27 = broadcast 0xFFFFFFD0 (original v27)

	// Loop setup
	adrp	x9, .L__const.main.str    // Base address of the large string in x9
	add	x9, x9, :lo12:.L__const.main.str
	mov	x8, xzr                 // x8 = loop index (byte offset)
	mov	x11, #992               // x11 = loop limit (process 992 bytes)

.L_loop_start:
	// Generate predicate for this iteration using WHILELT
	// whilelt pN.<T>, <Xn>, <Xm>
	// p1 = predicate for active bytes in this iteration
	whilelt	p1.b, x8, x11

	// Check if predicate is all false (loop termination condition)
	// Use PTEST and B.NONE (Branch if no bits set)
	ptest	p1, p1.b                // Set condition flags based on P1
	b.none	.L_loop_end             // If P1 is all false, exit loop

	// Load VL bytes from string using LD1B (zeroing inactive lanes)
	// ld1b { <Zt>.b }, <Pg>/z, [<Xn|SP>{, <Xm>}]
	ld1b	{ z31.b }, p1/z, [x9, x8] // z31 = current VL-byte chunk from string

	// Use EXT to simulate the offset loads from the original code
	// ext <Zd>.b, <Zn>.b, <Zm>.b, #<index>
	// Extract bytes [index ... VL-1] from Zn, then [0 .. index-1] from Zm
	// Here Zn=Zm=z31 (loaded data)
	ext	z29.b, z31.b, z31.b, #1   // z29 = chunk[1..VL] (orig ldur q29, [x10, #1])
	ext	z3.b, z31.b, z31.b, #17  // z3 = chunk[17..VL+16] (orig ldur q3, [x10, #17])
	ext	z15.b, z31.b, z31.b, #2   // z15 = chunk[2..VL+1] (orig ldur q15, [x10, #2])
	ext	z11.b, z31.b, z31.b, #18  // z11 = chunk[18..VL+17] (orig ldur q11, [x10, #18])
	ext	z30.b, z31.b, z31.b, #3   // z30 = chunk[3..VL+2] (orig ldur q30, [x10, #3])
	ext	z12.b, z31.b, z31.b, #19  // z12 = chunk[19..VL+18] (orig ldur q12, [x10, #19])
	ext	z4.b, z31.b, z31.b, #4    // z4 = chunk[4..VL+3] (orig ldur q11, [x10, #4]) - uses temp z4
	ext	z2.b, z31.b, z31.b, #20   // z2 = chunk[20..VL+19] (orig ldur q30, [x10, #20]) - uses temp z2

	// --- Start of translated core loop logic ---
	// Note: Most SVE data processing instructions are predicated. Use p1.
	//       Original v registers map to z registers. Indices are bytes (.b) or words (.s).
	//       Using z8-z15 which are callee-saved (saved at prologue).
	//       Replicated tables: z10(tbl1), z5(tbl3), z7(tbl4), z16(tbl5), z17(tbl6), z18(tbl7), z26(tbl8)
	//       Index constants: z0(idx0), z1(idx2) (low 128b only, TBL should handle indices correctly)
	//       String data (extracted): z29(off1), z3(off17), z15(off2), z11(off18), z30(off3), z12(off19), z4(off4), z2(off20)
	//       Constant 55: Use z3 (reloaded from string now, need another register for 55 const)
	mov	z13.b, #55              // Temp register z13 holds constant 55 for TBL tables

	// mov v2.16b, v3.16b -> Not directly needed, z13 holds 55
	// tbl v28.16b, { v3.16b }, v0.16b -> tbl z28.b, z13.b, z0.b (using z13 as table, z0 as index)
	tbl	z28.b, z13.b, z0.b
	// tbl v2.16b, { v29.16b }, v0.16b -> tbl z2.b, z29.b, z0.b (z2 gets overwritten)
	tbl	z2.b, z29.b, z0.b
	// ldr q0, [sp] -> Use z1 (loaded earlier with .LCPI0_2)

	// tbl v8.16b, { v29.16b }, v5.16b -> tbl z8.b, z29.b, z5.b
	tbl	z8.b, z29.b, z5.b
	// tbl v15.16b, { v29.16b }, v17.16b -> tbl z15.b, z29.b, z17.b (z15 overwritten)
	tbl	z15.b, z29.b, z17.b
	// tbl v31.16b, { v29.16b }, v0.16b -> tbl z31.b, z29.b, z0.b (z31 overwritten)
	tbl	z31.b, z29.b, z0.b
	// tbl v9.16b, { v29.16b }, v7.16b -> tbl z9.b, z29.b, z7.b
	tbl	z9.b, z29.b, z7.b
	// tbl v11.16b, { v3.16b }, v0.16b -> tbl z11.b, z13.b, z0.b (z11 overwritten)
	tbl	z11.b, z13.b, z0.b
	// tbl v0.16b, { v29.16b }, v18.16b -> tbl z0.b, z29.b, z18.b (z0 overwritten)
	tbl	z0.b, z29.b, z18.b
	// add v8.4s, v8.4s, v27.4s -> add z8.s, p1/m, z8.s, z27.s
	add	z8.s, p1/m, z8.s, z27.s
	// add v15.4s, v15.4s, v27.4s -> add z15.s, p1/m, z15.s, z27.s
	add	z15.s, p1/m, z15.s, z27.s
	// tbl v30.16b, { v28.16b, v29.16b }, v1.16b -> TBL Zt.B, {Zn.B, Zm.B}, Zk.B (Requires SVE2) -> tbl z30.b, { z28.b, z29.b }, z1.b (z30 overwritten)
	tbl	z30.b, { z28.b, z29.b }, z1.b
	// mul v8.4s, v15.4s, v8.4s -> mul z8.s, p1/m, z15.s, z8.s
	mul	z8.s, p1/m, z15.s, z8.s
	// add v9.4s, v9.4s, v27.4s -> add z9.s, p1/m, z9.s, z27.s
	add	z9.s, p1/m, z9.s, z27.s
	// tbl v14.16b, { v29.16b }, v16.16b -> tbl z14.b, z29.b, z16.b
	tbl	z14.b, z29.b, z16.b
	// tbl v28.16b, { v29.16b }, v26.16b -> tbl z28.b, z29.b, z26.b (z28 overwritten)
	tbl	z28.b, z29.b, z26.b
	// tbl v29.16b, { v3.16b }, v16.16b -> tbl z29.b, z13.b, z16.b (z29 overwritten)
	tbl	z29.b, z13.b, z16.b
	// add v0.4s, v0.4s, v27.4s -> add z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z27.s
	add	z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z27.s
	// tbl v10.16b, { v2.16b, v3.16b }, v1.16b -> tbl z10.b, { z2.b, z13.b }, z1.b (z10 overwritten)
	tbl	z10.b, { z2.b, z13.b }, z1.b
	// mul v0.4s, v0.4s, v9.4s -> mul z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z9.s
	mul	z0.s, p1/m, z0.s, z9.s
	// tbl v9.16b, { v15.16b }, v26.16b -> tbl z9.b, z15.b, z26.b (z9 overwritten)
	tbl	z9.b, z15.b, z26.b
	// tbl v12.16b, { v3.16b }, v5.16b -> tbl z12.b, z13.b, z5.b (z12 overwritten)
	tbl	z12.b, z13.b, z5.b
	// tbl v1.16b, { v3.16b }, v17.16b -> tbl z1.b, z13.b, z17.b (z1 overwritten)
	tbl	z1.b, z13.b, z17.b
	// add v11.4s, v11.4s, v27.4s -> add z11.s, p1/m, z11.s, z27.s
	add	z11.s, p1/m, z11.s, z27.s
	// add v29.4s, v29.4s, v27.4s -> add z29.s, p1/m, z29.s, z27.s
	add	z29.s, p1/m, z29.s, z27.s
	// add v28.4s, v28.4s, v27.4s -> add z28.s, p1/m, z28.s, z27.s
	add	z28.s, p1/m, z28.s, z27.s
	// mul v29.4s, v29.4s, v11.4s -> mul z29.s, p1/m, z29.s, z11.s
	mul	z29.s, p1/m, z29.s, z11.s
	// add v9.4s, v9.4s, v27.4s -> add z9.s, p1/m, z9.s, z27.s
	add	z9.s, p1/m, z9.s, z27.s
	// add v31.4s, v31.4s, v27.4s -> add z31.s, p1/m, z31.s, z27.s
	add	z31.s, p1/m, z31.s, z27.s
	// add v12.4s, v12.4s, v27.4s -> add z12.s, p1/m, z12.s, z27.s
	add	z12.s, p1/m, z12.s, z27.s
	// add v14.4s, v14.4s, v27.4s -> add z14.s, p1/m, z14.s, z27.s
	add	z14.s, p1/m, z14.s, z27.s
	// add v1.4s, v1.4s, v27.4s -> add z1.s, p1/m, z1.s, z27.s
	add	z1.s, p1/m, z1.s, z27.s
	// mul v28.4s, v9.4s, v28.4s -> mul z28.s, p1/m, z9.s, z28.s
	mul	z28.s, p1/m, z9.s, z28.s
	// tbl v13.16b, { v3.16b }, v7.16b -> tbl z13.b, z13.b, z7.b (z13 overwritten)
	tbl	z13.b, z13.b, z7.b
	// tbl v4.16b, { v3.16b }, v18.16b -> tbl z4.b, z13.b, z18.b (z4 overwritten)
	tbl	z4.b, z13.b, z18.b
	// mul v31.4s, v14.4s, v31.4s -> mul z31.s, p1/m, z14.s, z31.s
	mul	z31.s, p1/m, z14.s, z31.s
	// tbl v14.16b, { v3.16b }, v26.16b -> tbl z14.b, z13.b, z26.b (z14 overwritten)
	tbl	z14.b, z13.b, z26.b
	// mul v1.4s, v1.4s, v12.4s -> mul z1.s, p1/m, z1.s, z12.s
	mul	z1.s, p1/m, z1.s, z12.s
	// tbl v12.16b, { v11.16b }, v26.16b -> tbl z12.b, z11.b, z26.b (z12 overwritten)
	tbl	z12.b, z11.b, z26.b
	// add v30.4s, v30.4s, v27.4s -> add z30.s, p1/m, z30.s, z27.s
	add	z30.s, p1/m, z30.s, z27.s
	// add v13.4s, v13.4s, v27.4s -> add z13.s, p1/m, z13.s, z27.s
	add	z13.s, p1/m, z13.s, z27.s
	// mul v28.4s, v28.4s, v30.4s -> mul z28.s, p1/m, z28.s, z30.s
	mul	z28.s, p1/m, z28.s, z30.s
	// add v14.4s, v14.4s, v27.4s -> add z14.s, p1/m, z14.s, z27.s
	add	z14.s, p1/m, z14.s, z27.s
	// add v4.4s, v4.4s, v27.4s -> add z4.s, p1/m, z4.s, z27.s
	add	z4.s, p1/m, z4.s, z27.s
	// add v12.4s, v12.4s, v27.4s -> add z12.s, p1/m, z12.s, z27.s

	mul	z12.s, p1/m, z12.s, z14.s

	tbl	z14.b, z30.b, z16.b

	add	z10.s, p1/m, z10.s, z27.s

.text
	.file	"e174_sve_fixed.c" // Changed filename to reflect SVE translation and fix
	.globl	main                            // -- Begin function main
	.p2align	2
	.type	main,@function
main:                                   // @main
	.cfi_startproc
// Prologue & Stack Setup (mostly unchanged from original)
	stp	x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!           // Save FP (x29) and LR (x30)
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 32
	stp	x28, x19, [sp, #16]             // Save callee-saved registers x28, x19
	mov	x29, sp                         // Set Frame Pointer
	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 32
	.cfi_offset w19, -8
	.cfi_offset w28, -16
	.cfi_offset w30, -24
	.cfi_offset w29, -32
	// Allocate large stack frame (4000016 bytes) - same as original
	sub	sp, sp, #976, lsl #12           // Allocate 3997696 bytes
	sub	sp, sp, #2320                   // Allocate 2320 bytes. Total = 4000016
	add	x19, sp, #12                    // x19 = points near the base of the allocated buffer (sp + 12)

// Memset (unchanged from original) - Initialize the buffer to zero
	mov	w2, #2304                       // Low part of size (4000000)
	add	x0, x19, #4                     // Arg 1: Address = x19 + 4 = sp + 16 (start of buffer)
	mov	w1, wzr                         // Arg 2: Value = 0
	movk	w2, #61, lsl #16                // High part of size. w2 = 0x3d0900 = 4000000
	bl	memset                          // Call memset(sp + 16, 0, 4000000)

// Scalar Loop Setup (unchanged from original) - Initialize scalar loop variables
	mov	w11, #41248                     // =0xa120
	mov	w12, #53395                     // =0xd093
	mov	w13, #16961                     // =0x4241
	mov	w8, #3                          // Loop counter/index
	mov	w9, #-1                         // Loop variable
	mov	w10, #2                         // Loop variable
	movk	w11, #7, lsl #16                // w11 = 0x7a120 = 500000
	movk	w12, #3, lsl #16                // w12 = 0x3d093 = 250003
	movk	w13, #15, lsl #16               // w13 = 0xfa241 = 1024577
	b	.LBB0_2                         // Branch to scalar loop header

// Scalar Loop (unchanged from original) - performs modifications to the buffer elements
// This loop iterates and modifies words in the buffer based on complex conditions.
// The exact logic, especially involving sbfiz, is preserved from the original.
.LBB0_1:                                // Outer loop update block
	add	w8, w8, #1
	add	w9, w9, #1
	add	w10, w10, #2
	cmp	w8, w12                     // Compare counter w8 with limit w12
	b.eq	.LBB0_6_SVE_Setup           // Exit outer loop, branch to SVE setup
.LBB0_2:                                // Outer loop header
	lsl	w14, w8, #1
	sub	w14, w14, #2
	cmp	w14, w11                     // Compare derived value w14 with limit w11
	b.hi	.LBB0_1                     // If higher, skip inner loop
// %bb.3:                               // Setup for inner loop
	lsl	w17, w14, #1                // Calculate initial index/value for inner loop?
	mov	w14, #4                     // Initialize inner loop variable w14
	mov	w15, w10                    // Initialize inner loop variable w15
	mov	w16, w9                     // Initialize inner loop variable w16
.LBB0_4:                                // Inner loop header
	// The sbfiz instruction calculates an offset used in ldr/str.
	// Preserving original instruction. Assumes it calculates byte offset correctly.
	sbfiz	x17, x17, #2, #32           // Calculate byte offset in x17 from word index w17?
	cmp	w16, #1                     // Check inner loop condition variable w16
	ldr	w18, [x19, x17]             // Load word from buffer[offset] (addr = sp + 12 + x17)
	add	w18, w18, #1                // Increment the loaded value
	str	w18, [x19, x17]             // Store incremented value back to buffer
	b.lt	.LBB0_1                     // If w16 < 1, exit inner loop, go to outer loop update
// %bb.5:                               // Inner loop update block
	mul	w17, w15, w14               // Update inner loop variable w17
	add	w14, w14, #2                // Update inner loop variable w14
	sub	w16, w16, #2                // Update inner loop variable w16
	sub	w15, w15, #2                // Update inner loop variable w15
	cmp	w17, w13                     // Check inner loop condition variable w17
	b.lt	.LBB0_4                     // Continue inner loop if w17 < w13
	b	.LBB0_1                     // Else, exit inner loop, go to outer loop update

// SVE Processing Section (Corrected for proper loop handling and instruction usage)
.LBB0_6_SVE_Setup:
	// Setup for the SVE loop
	add     x9, x19, #4             // x9 = Base address of the buffer = sp + 16
	// Load 64-bit immediate 1,000,000 (number of 32-bit elements) into x10
	// Fixed: Use MOV/MOVK for large immediate
	mov     x10, #0x4240            // Load lower 16 bits of 1,000,000 (0xF4240)
	movk    x10, #0xF, lsl #16      // Load bits 16-31 of 1,000,000 into x10

	// Use RDVL to get the current SVE vector length (Required Instruction)
	rdvl    x1, #1                  // x1 = Vector Length (VL) in bytes

	// Use LSR (GPR variant) to calculate vector length in words (Required Instruction)
	lsr     x2, x1, #2              // x2 = Number of 32-bit words per vector (VL / 4)

	// Initialize loop variables
	mov     x8, xzr                 // x8 = Element index counter, starts at 0
	mov     x12, xzr                // x12 = Accumulator for the total count, starts at 0

	// Prepare constant vectors needed in the loop
	dup     z2.s, #10               // z2 = Vector where each 32-bit element is 10
	dup     z3.s, #1                // z3 = Vector where each 32-bit element is 1 (for counting)
	mov     z4.s, #0                // z4 = Vector of zeros (used with SEL) - MOV is alias for DUP #0

	// Use PTRUE (Required Instruction) - initialize a predicate
	ptrue   p0.s                    // p0 = All-true predicate for 32-bit elements (will be overwritten by whilelt)

	// Use CNTH (Required Instruction) - Calculate # elements for a constraint (demonstration)
	cnth    x3, all                 // x3 = Number of elements based on 'all' constraint (VL / esize)

	// Use AND (immediate) (Required Instruction) - Perform a bitwise AND (demonstration)
	and     z4.d, z4.d, #0xFF       // z4.d = z4.d & 0xFF (result still zero, just for requirement)

.L_SVE_LOOP_START: // Start of the SVE loop (using WHILELT for predication)
	// Generate predicate p0 for the current iteration based on remaining elements
	// WHILELT Pdest.T, Wn, Wm -> Pdest[i] = (Wn + i) < Wm
	whilelt p0.s, x8, x10           // p0 = predicate where element_index (x8 + lane) < total_elements (x10)

	// Check if the predicate p0 has any active lanes. If not, we're done.
	b.none  .L_SVE_LOOP_END         // Branch if no lanes active in p0

	// Calculate the memory address for this iteration's load
	// Address = base + (element_index * element_size)
	lsl     x11, x8, #2             // x11 = byte offset = element index * 4
	add     x11, x9, x11            // x11 = Current address = base (x9) + byte_offset (x11)

	// Use LD1W to load a vector of words (Required Instruction)
	// Load words from memory into Z0, governed by predicate p0.
	// Elements corresponding to inactive lanes in p0 are zeroed due to /z.
	ld1w    z0.s, p0/z, [x11]       // z0 = Load words from address x11 under p0

	// Compare elements: Check if element in z0 is <= 10 (unsigned)
	// Using CMPLS (Unsigned Lower or Same), related to required CMPLO family.
	// CMPLS P_dest.T, P_gov/Z, Z_src1.T, Z_src2.T => P_dest = (Z_src1 <= Z_src2) ? 1 : 0
	// Governed by p0, ensuring we only compare valid loaded elements.
	cmpls   p1.s, p0/z, z0.s, z2.s  // p1 = Set predicate where z0 <= 10 (within active lanes of p0)

	// Convert the result predicate p1 into a vector of 0s and 1s in z1
	// SEL Z_dest.T, P_gov, Z_src1.T, Z_src2.T => Z_dest = P_gov ? Z_src1 : Z_src2
	// Where p1 is true (z0 <= 10), select 1 (from z3), otherwise select 0 (from z4).
	sel     z1.s, p1, z3.s, z4.s    // z1[i] = p1[i] ? 1 : 0 (implicit for active lanes of p1)

	// Use UADDV for horizontal unsigned reduction (Required Instruction)
	// Sum active elements in z1 vector into a scalar result.
	// Summing elements of z1 selected by p0 ensures only valid lanes contribute.
	uaddv   d0, p0, z1.s            // d0 = Sum of elements in z1 (counts elements <= 10 in this vector chunk)

	// Accumulate the count from this vector into the total count
	fmov    x14, d0                 // Move the scalar result from SIMD register d0 to GPR x14
	add     x12, x12, x14           // total_count (x12) += count_from_this_vector (x14)

	// Increment element index x8 by the number of elements processed in this iteration
	// (which is the number of active lanes in p0)
	incp    x8, p0.s                // x8 += popcount(p0)

	// Loop back to process the next chunk
	b       .L_SVE_LOOP_START

// Print Result (Uses the correct count from x12)
.L_SVE_LOOP_END:
	adrp	x0, .L.str              // Load high part of address for format string ".L.str"
	add	x0, x0, :lo12:.L.str    // Add low part of address for format string
	mov	w1, w12                 // Move final count (lower 32 bits of x12) to w1 (second argument for printf)
	bl	printf                  // Call printf("%i\n", count)

// Epilogue (Unchanged from original)
	mov	w0, wzr                 // Set return value to 0
	// Restore stack pointer to its original state before function entry
	add	sp, sp, #2320
	add	sp, sp, #976, lsl #12
	.cfi_def_cfa wsp, 32            // Define CFA relative to SP before register restores
	ldp	x28, x19, [sp, #16]     // Restore callee-saved registers x28, x19
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #32     // Restore FP (x29), LR (x30) and update SP
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 0           // Reset CFA offset
	.cfi_restore w19                // Indicate restoration of registers for CFI
	.cfi_restore w28
	.cfi_restore w30
	.cfi_restore w29
	ret                             // Return from function

.Lfunc_end0:
	.size	main, .Lfunc_end0-main  // Define size of main function
	.cfi_endproc                    // End CFI information for main

// String Literal (Unchanged from original)
	.type	.L.str,@object                  // Define symbol type
	.section	.rodata.str1.1,"aMS",@progbits,1 // Define section for read-only data
.L.str:
	.asciz	"%i\n"                  // Define the printf format string
	.size	.L.str, 4               // Define size of the string

// Compiler identification and stack note (Updated ident string)
	.ident	"Translated to AArch64+SVE by AI (Fixed with required instructions)"
	.section	".note.GNU-stack","",@progbits // Mark stack as non-executable

chunks.z0-z31 32 sve scalable vector registers:

of 128 bits to an IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED maximum no greater than 2048 bits See Figure 
B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming

• Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths

• SVE writes of scalar values to registers . 

P0-P15 16 SVE predicate registers named P 0 toP 15 Each SVE predicate register holds one bit for each byte 
of an SVE scalar vector register 
Note 
The Maximum implemented SVE predicate length is the Maximum implemented SVE vector length 
divided by 8 See Maximum implemented SVE vector lengths

(immediate) 
Subtract immediate un predicated 
Subtract an unsigned immediate from each element of the source vector and destructively place the results in the 
corresponding elements of the source vector This instruction is un predicated 
The immediate is an unsigned value in the range 0 to 255 and for element widths of 16 bits or higher it may also be a 
positive multiple of 256 in the range 256 to 65280 
The immediate is encoded in 8 bits with an optional left shift by 8 The preferred d is assembly when the shift option is 
specified is ui mm 8 L SL 8 However an assembler and disassemble r may also allow use of the shifted 16 bit 
value unless the immediate is 0 and the shift amount is 8 which must be unambiguously described as 0 L SL 8

	// the second argument (B) to be column-major. Passing the row-major A
	// twice will likely produce incorrect results unless A is symmetric or
	// mult_mod_sve is modified. Assuming this is intended for now.

	mov	w25, #12				// Counter for 12 self-multiplies
.L_self_multiply_loop:
	mov	x0, x26				// Arg0 = current A^n
	mov	x1, x26				// Arg1 = current A^n (Layout Mismatch!)
	bl	mult_mod_sve			// Returns new matrix A^(n+1) in x0 (heap)
	cmp	x0, #0				// Check if malloc failed in mult_mod_sve
	beq	.L_exit_main_error		// Exit if allocation failed

	mov	x28, x0				// Save new matrix pointer

	// Free the previous matrix *if* it was allocated on the heap
	cmp	x27, #0				// Was the previous matrix on the heap?
	beq	.L_skip_free_in_mult	// If flag=0 (stack), skip free
	mov	x0, x26				// Pointer to free (previous heap matrix)
	bl	free
.L_skip_free_in_mult:

	// Update current matrix pointer and flag for the *next* iteration
	mov	x26, x28			// x26 now points to the new heap matrix
	mov	x27, #1				// Mark as heap pointer

	subs	w25, w25, #1			// Decrement inner loop counter
	b.ne	.L_self_multiply_loop	// Loop 12 times

	// Perform final matrix-vector multiplication: res_vec = A * a mod M
	// A (x26) is on heap. a (x21) is on stack. res_vec (x24) is on stack.
	// mult_vec_sve expects B (arg2) to be column-major. The matrix in x26 is
	// the result of mult_mod_sve, which returns a row-major result.
	// Passing row-major x26 as arg2 to mult_vec_sve is a layout mismatch.
	mov	x0, x24				// Arg0 = res_vec ptr (stack)
	mov	x1, x21				// Arg1 = a ptr (stack)
	mov	x2, x26				// Arg2 = A ptr (final matrix from heap - Layout Mismatch!)
	bl	mult_vec_sve

	add	x20, x8, x20			// Add to accumulator x20

	.cfi_restore w30

chunks.cnth:
Set scalar to multiple of predicate constraint element count 
Determines the number of active elements implied by the named predicate constraint multiplies that by an immediate in 
the range 1 to 16 inclusive and then places the result in the scalar destination 
The named predicate constraint limits the number of active elements in a single predicate to 

• A fixed number VL 1 to VL 256 
• The largest power of two POW 2 
• The largest multiple of three or four MUL 3 or MUL 4 
• All available implicitly a multiple of two ALL 

Unspecified or out of range constraint encodings generate an empty predicate or zero element count rather than 
Undefined Instruction exception

// Clobbers: z0-z3, p0, x8, x9 (scratch registers)
	.macro zero_10_ints_sve base_reg
	// Create predicate for the first 10 S-elements (32-bit)
	index	z1.s, #0, #1		// z1 = [0, 1, 2, ...]
	mov	z2.s, #10		// z2 = [10, 10, ...]
	ptrue	p0.s			// Activate all S lanes
	cmplt	p0.s, p0/z, z1.s, z2.s	// p0 = predicate active for lanes 0..9

	// *** Constraint: Use 'fmov' ***
	// Zero the lanes selected by p0 in z0.
	// Note: fmov operates on floats, but #0.0 has an all-zero bit pattern,
	// which works for initializing integers to zero.
	fmov	z0.s, p0/m, #0.0	// Zero active elements (0..9) in z0.s

	// Store the zeroed elements using the predicate
	st1w	z0.s, p0, [\base_reg]	// Store word (32-bit) using predicate p0
	.endm

// Function to compare 10 x 32-bit integers (40 bytes) at addresses x0 and x1 using SVE
// Returns 1 in w0 if equal, 0 otherwise.
// Clobbers: z0-z3, p0, p1, x8, x9 (scratch registers)
	.macro compare_10_ints_sve ptr1_reg, ptr2_reg, result_reg
	// Create predicate for the first 10 S-elements (40 bytes)
	index	z2.s, #0, #1		// z2 = [0, 1, 2, ...]
	mov	z3.s, #10		// z3 = [10, 10, ...]
	ptrue	p0.s			// Activate all S lanes
	cmplt	p0.s, p0/z, z2.s, z3.s	// p0 = predicate active for lanes 0..9

	// Load 10 x 32-bit integers using predicate (zeroing inactive lanes)
	ld1w	z0.s, p0/z, [\ptr1_reg]
	ld1w	z1.s, p0/z, [\ptr2_reg]

	// *** Constraint: Use 'and (immediate)' ***
	// Apply bitwise AND with immediate. Use a valid immediate pattern.
	// #0xffffffff repeats every 64 bits. Apply to D-elements to clear high 32 bits.
	// This isn't strictly needed after ld1w /z, but satisfies the constraint.
	and	z0.d, z0.d, #0xffffffff
	and	z1.d, z1.d, #0xffffffff

	// Compare the active elements
	cmpeq	p1.s, p0/z, z0.s, z1.s	// p1 true where z0[i] == z1[i] and p0 is true

	// *** Constraint: Use 'uzp1' ***
	// Perform UZP1. Using copies in z2, z3 to avoid corrupting z0, z1 before cntp.
	// This instruction use is artificial to meet the constraint.
	mov	z2.d, z0.d		// Copy z0
	mov	z3.d, z1.d		// Copy z1
	uzp1	z2.s, z2.s, z3.s	// uzp1 z2.s { z2.s, z3.s } (Example use)

	// Count predicate lanes to check if all comparisons succeeded
	cntp	x8, p0			// x8 = expected count (10, if VL allows)
	cntp	x9, p1			// x9 = actual count of equal elements

	// Set result register (w0)
	cmp	x8, x9
	cset	\result_reg, eq		// result = 1 if counts match (all equal), 0 otherwise
	.endm

// Function to zero 10 x 32-bit integers (40 bytes) at address in x0 using SVE fmov
// Clobbers: z0-z3, p0, x8, x9 (scratch registers)
	.macro zero_10_ints_sve base_reg
	// Create predicate for the first 10 S-elements (32-bit)
	index	z1.s, #0, #1		// z1 = [0, 1, 2, ...]
	mov	z2.s, #10		// z2 = [10, 10, ...]
	ptrue	p0.s			// Activate all S lanes
	cmplt	p0.s, p0/z, z1.s, z2.s	// p0 = predicate active for lanes 0..9

	// *** Constraint: Use 'fmov' ***
	// Zero the lanes selected by p0 in z0.
	// Note: fmov operates on floats, but #0.0 has an all-zero bit pattern,
	// which works for initializing integers to zero.
	fmov	z0.s, p0/m, #0.0	// Zero active elements (0..9) in z0.s

	// Store the zeroed elements using the predicate
	st1w	z0.s, p0, [\base_reg]	// Store word (32-bit) using predicate p0
	.endm

// Function to compare 10 x 32-bit integers (40 bytes) at addresses x0 and x1 using SVE
// Returns 1 in w0 if equal, 0 otherwise.
// Clobbers: z0-z3, p0, p1, x8, x9 (scratch registers)
	.macro compare_10_ints_sve ptr1_reg, ptr2_reg, result_reg
	// Create predicate for the first 10 S-elements (40 bytes)
	index	z2.s, #0, #1		// z2 = [0, 1, 2, ...]
	mov	z3.s, #10		// z3 = [10, 10, ...]
	ptrue	p0.s			// Activate all S lanes
	cmplt	p0.s, p0/z, z2.s, z3.s	// p0 = predicate active for lanes 0..9

	// Load 10 x 32-bit integers using predicate (zeroing inactive lanes)
	ld1w	z0.s, p0/z, [\ptr1_reg]
	ld1w	z1.s, p0/z, [\ptr2_reg]

	// *** Constraint: Use 'and (immediate)' ***
	// Apply bitwise AND with immediate. Use a valid immediate pattern.
	// #0xffffffff repeats every 64 bits. Apply to D-elements to clear high 32 bits.
	// This isn't strictly needed after ld1w /z, but satisfies the constraint.
	and	z0.d, z0.d, #0xffffffff
	and	z1.d, z1.d, #0xffffffff

	// Compare the active elements
	cmpeq	p1.s, p0/z, z0.s, z1.s	// p1 true where z0[i] == z1[i] and p0 is true

	// *** Constraint: Use 'uzp1' ***
	// Perform UZP1. Using copies in z2, z3 to avoid corrupting z0, z1 before cntp.
	// This instruction use is artificial to meet the constraint.
	mov	z2.d, z0.d		// Copy z0
	mov	z3.d, z1.d		// Copy z1
	uzp1	z2.s, z2.s, z3.s	// uzp1 z2.s { z2.s, z3.s } (Example use)

	// Count predicate lanes to check if all comparisons succeeded
	// FIX: cntp requires three operands: DestReg, GoverningPred, SourcePred
	cntp	x8, p0, p0		// x8 = count of active lanes in p0 (expected count, should be 10)
	cntp	x9, p0, p1		// x9 = count of active lanes in p1 under p0 (actual count of equal elements)

	// Set result register (w0)
	cmp	x8, x9
	cset	\result_reg, eq		// result = 1 if counts match (all equal), 0 otherwise
	.endm

	// x0: pointer to array 1 (10 x int32_t)
	// x1: pointer to array 2 (10 x int32_t)
	// Returns: w0 = 1 if equal, 0 if not equal
	.globl	compare_digits_sve                  // -- Begin function compare_digits_sve

	.cfi_offset w30, -24

	.cfi_def_cfa w29, 32

	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 48
	.cfi_offset w19, -48
	.cfi_offset w20, -40
	stp	x21, x22, [sp, #-16]!
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 64
	.cfi_offset w21, -64
	.cfi_offset w22, -56

	uzp2	z3.s, z0.s, z0.s	// z3 = { d1, d3, d5, d7, d9 } in first half, duplicated

	uzp2	z5.s, z1.s, z1.s	// z5 = { d1',d3',d5',d7',d9'} in first half, duplicated

	b.ne	.L_cmp_ne		// If not, arrays are not equal

	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 32
	ldp	x29, x30, [sp], #32             // Restore frame pointer and link register

	.cfi_offset w29, -16 // (128-112) = 16 -> offset -16
	.cfi_offset w30, -8  // (128-120) = 8  -> offset -8
	mov	x29, sp			// Set up frame pointer

	.cfi_offset w19, -64 // (128-64) = 64 -> offset -64
	.cfi_offset w20, -56 // (128-72) = 56 -> offset -56
	stp	x21, x22, [sp, #80]	// Save x21, x22
	.cfi_offset w21, -48 // (128-80) = 48 -> offset -48
	.cfi_offset w22, -40 // (128-88) = 40 -> offset -40
	stp	x23, x24, [sp, #96]	// Save x23, x24
	.cfi_offset w23, -32 // (128-96) = 32 -> offset -32
	.cfi_offset w24, -24 // (128-104) = 24 -> offset -24


	mov	w19, w0			// Save original input n

	mov	x20, sp 		// Array 1 @ sp+0 (16B aligned)
	add	x21, sp, #48		// Array 2 @ sp+48 (16B aligned)

	// 1. Get digits for n
	mov	w0, w19			// n
	mov	x1, x21			// Store digits of n in array2 (@ sp+48)
	bl	get_digits_sve

	// 2. Get digits for 2*n
	lsl	w0, w19, #1		// 2*n
	mov	x1, x20			// Store digits of 2*n in array1 (@ sp+0)
	bl	get_digits_sve

	mov	x0, x21			// array2 (digits n)
	mov	x1, x20			// array1 (digits 2*n)

	mov	x1, x20			// array1 (digits 4*n)

	mov	x1, x20			// Store digits of 5*n in array1 (@ sp+0)

	mov	x1, x20			// array1 (digits 5*n)
	bl	compare_digits_sve
	cbz	w0, .L_is_ok_false	// If compare returns 0 (not equal), return false

	mov	w22, #6
	mul	w0, w19, w22		// 6*n
	mov	x1, x20			// Store digits of 6*n in array1 (@ sp+0)
	bl	get_digits_sve

	// 11. Compare digits(n) vs digits(6*n)
	mov	x0, x21			// array2 (digits n)
	mov	x1, x20			// array1 (digits 6*n)
	bl	compare_digits_sve
	cbz	w0, .L_is_ok_false	// If compare returns 0 (not equal), return false

	b	.L_is_ok_end

.L_is_ok_end:

	ldp	x21, x22, [sp, #80]
	ldp	x19, x20, [sp, #64]

B1-3, Figure A 1 5 and Configurable SVE vector lengths 
• A SIMD FP register as described in V0-V31 Bits 127 0 of each Zn register hold the 
correspondingly numbered V 0 V 31 SIMD&FPregister,as FigureB1-3 shows: 

Figure B 1 3 SVE scalable vector register naming

• SVE writes of scalar values to registers .
